lessons.title: Figures, axes and readable measurement
lessons.motivation: A chart encodes measurements and a question; axes and units are part of its truthfulness.
lessons.progression: Plot ordered predictions, then swap axes/units or an unordered customer sequence.
lessons.terms: Figure, Axes, plot, title, x/y label, units, legend, scale.
lessons.worked: With area [1,2,3], age held at 10, weights [100,−2] and bias 50, predictions are [130,230,330] (₹ lakh). Labeling the price axis rupees rather than ₹ lakh changes the communicated meaning.
lessons.misconception: An unlabeled line is not self-explanatory; the code variable name is not an axis label.

objectives.outcome: Match Figure/Axes roles to a supplied Matplotlib program.
objectives.assessment: Choose where plot and labeling methods belong.
objectives.remediation: Annotate the small fig, ax creation trace.

objectives.outcome: Choose correct coordinates, units and truthful series labels.
objectives.assessment: Repair swapped axes/unit labels and explain the consequence.
objectives.remediation: Map each axis back to the input table.

objectives.outcome: Predict a line plot only when order/continuity is justified.
objectives.assessment: Reject a line through arbitrarily ordered customers.
objectives.remediation: Compare row order with the intended independent variable.

objectives.outcome: Provide non-color-only labels and a numerical alternative.
objectives.assessment: Select a usable legend/marker/table combination.
objectives.remediation: Read the chart using only its textual description.

lessons.title: Histograms show distributions, not individual paths
lessons.motivation: Histograms aggregate intervals; probability is area when density is used.
lessons.progression: Predict two bins, then change widths or include an outlier.
lessons.terms: histogram, bin edge, count, density, bin width, outlier.
lessons.math: Frequency versus density; area rather than height for unequal widths.
lessons.worked: For ages [0,1,2,3] with bins [0,2,4], counts are [2,2]. In density mode with width 2 each height is .25 and total area is 1.
lessons.misconception: Density height is not bin probability unless width is one; changing bins changes appearance.

objectives.outcome: Predict bin membership including the final right edge convention.
objectives.assessment: Select counts for a changed bounded dataset.
objectives.remediation: Place values in labeled half-open bins, final bin right-inclusive.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish count, density height and probability area.
objectives.assessment: Repair a density-as-probability claim and justify using width.
objectives.remediation: Multiply each density height by bin width.

objectives.outcome: Explain the effect of bins and outliers on interpretation.
objectives.assessment: Choose a cautious conclusion after a bin change.
objectives.remediation: Compare the same raw values under both plots.

objectives.outcome: Choose a histogram for a quantitative distribution rather than a relationship.
objectives.assessment: Select a plot matching a new distribution question.
objectives.remediation: State whether one variable or paired variables are being studied.

lessons.title: Scatterplots, relationships and causal caution
lessons.motivation: The same observational pattern can support different intervention predictions.
lessons.progression: Compare paired/subgroup points and a causal counterexample.
lessons.terms: scatter, association, confounder, subgroup, overplotting, intervention.
lessons.math: Correlation, nonlinear association and observational versus causal effects.
lessons.worked: A supplied table has training_hours and score rising together while prior_experience differs by subgroup. A fitted line or colored groups alone cannot identify the effect of an extra hour.
lessons.misconception: A persuasive scatterplot or a large correlation is not causal evidence; zero correlation need not mean no relationship.

objectives.outcome: Preserve paired observations and inspect shape/outliers.
objectives.assessment: Reject a separately sorted x/y chart.
objectives.remediation: Reconnect points by row ID.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish association from an identified intervention effect.
objectives.assessment: Reject a causal claim and choose the missing design/assumption explanation.
objectives.remediation: Return to Statistics common-cause/intervention contrasts.

objectives.outcome: Recognize subgroup confounding and nonlinear patterns.
objectives.assessment: Choose interpretations of pooled versus grouped/curved cases.
objectives.remediation: Compare group membership and within-group patterns.

objectives.outcome: Use labels/markers and point tables to avoid color-only meaning.
objectives.assessment: Select a readable small scatter design.
objectives.remediation: Trace one named observation through the numerical alternative.

lessons.title: Box plots summarize spread with conventions
lessons.motivation: A box plot is a convention-dependent summary, not a verdict on which data to discard.
lessons.progression: Rebuild quartiles/fences, then compare a valid extreme observation.
lessons.terms: median, quartile, IQR, whisker, outlier, quantile method.
lessons.math: Five-number-style summaries; plotted outliers are not automatic data errors.
lessons.worked: For [1,2,3,4,5,20] with the pinned linear quantile method, Q1=2.25, median=3.5, Q3=4.75; IQR=2.5 and 20 lies beyond the upper 1.5-IQR fence.
lessons.misconception: The box center is not necessarily the mean; whiskers are not always min/max; an outlier marker does not justify deletion.

objectives.outcome: Interpret box, whiskers and marked observations using the stated convention.
objectives.assessment: Label a changed plot from a matching summary table.
objectives.remediation: Rebuild the plot from ordered values and fences.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish median/IQR from mean/standard deviation.
objectives.assessment: Repair a mislabeled summary and explain robustness.
objectives.remediation: Compare definitions and units in Statistics recall.

objectives.outcome: Assess outlier influence without automatically removing observations.
objectives.assessment: Choose an investigation rather than unsupported deletion.
objectives.remediation: Compare provenance and summaries with/without the point.

objectives.outcome: Compare group summaries without claiming equal sample sizes or causation.
objectives.assessment: Select a limited conclusion with group counts shown.
objectives.remediation: Inspect counts and the unaggregated value tables.

lessons.title: Choose charts and detect misleading claims
lessons.motivation: Scale choices change perception without changing the underlying measured difference.
lessons.progression: Compare disclosed axes/bins and repair a misleading conclusion.
lessons.terms: truncated axis, shared scale, cherry-picking, normalization, exploratory analysis.
lessons.math: Scale invariance of values versus perceptual differences; exploratory evidence is not confirmatory proof.
lessons.worked: Two lines ending at 100 and 102 can look dramatically different on an axis [99,103]. A zoomed axis may reveal detail, but its limits and absolute difference must be explicit.
lessons.misconception: A truncated axis is not automatically forbidden, but hiding its range or mixing scales can mislead; appearance is not effect size.

objectives.outcome: Detect misleading scale/denominator choices and propose a transparent repair.
objectives.assessment: Choose a repair plus absolute-unit explanation for a new chart.
objectives.remediation: Compare identical data under disclosed common scales.

objectives.outcome: Select line/scatter/histogram/box plot for a stated ML question.
objectives.assessment: Match a new diagnostic question to a chart and rationale.
objectives.remediation: Identify time/order, pairing or distribution first.

objectives.outcome: Separate descriptive visual evidence from generalization claims.
objectives.assessment: Reject a chart-based claim of unseen-data performance.
objectives.remediation: Trace which rows the plot actually contains.

objectives.outcome: Explain why exploratory pattern hunting needs later validation (introductory).
objectives.assessment: Choose a cautious follow-up rather than proof from a selected pattern.
objectives.remediation: Distinguish exploration from a predeclared evaluation.

values = np.array([4.0, 6.0, 8.0, 10.0, 12.0, 42.0], dtype=float)
